verdict.rationale: Netlify plugs into existing Git workflows: it auto-deploys on every push, gives each PR a preview URL, and can start a project from a Git repository. Users confirm the GitHub integration and npm builds work, and the integrations directory shows starters for SvelteKit, Angular and Remix. However, nothing shows it fitting into an existing CI pipeline or editor. Community reports also show Netlify-specific config (a netlify.toml [dev] section, Netlify redirects mirrored in nginx for parity), which cuts against the "no proprietary tooling" part of the story. missing for 10: documented use with existing third-party CI pipelines, any editor workflow integration, evidence that no Netlify-specific config (netlify.toml/redirects) is needed, broader framework-agnostic documentation.

support.subject: As a developer, I can keep using my existing Git, CI, editor, and framework workflows without adopting proprietary tooling

citations.quote: Auto-deploy on every push. Every PR gets a preview URL.
